observations.finding: The optic stack reads as a projecting concentric mechanical target, and the surrounding orbital/cheek masses as broad smooth pieces. The crown reads as a regular radial fan of large blades. Compared with the scoped July head and candidate03, the optic/cheek/crown framing does not yet reproduce the dense irregular swept plating around a deep convex hook and open cheek/mandible. The open jaw gap is visible; lack of jaw opening is not the finding.

The authored model reads as a symmetrical armored pear with a long, narrow upright neck. Candidate03 reads as a more compact curved neck-to-deep-breast connection; the torso courses in the model are highly regular scallops. The rear render makes bilateral shoulder pods and straight dorsal neck framing especially clear.

The mantle is continuous and substantially covered, but reads as an evenly scaled detachable oval shield rather than a tapered sweep integrated into the flank. This is a shape/integration/pattern difference, not a coverage-area deficit.

eraContinuity.finding: Maker and Mechanic keep the optic dark; amber illumination is present only in Advanced, consistent with the stated era distinction.

Maker finish appears cleaner and lighter than the selected Maker clean illustration. Treat this only as a scoped finish discrepancy to assess against the newly made state; it is not a directive to add centuries of patina.

Mechanic three-quarter shows no clearly legible localized repair feature in this fixed pose and retains a material/geometry impression close to Advanced, while the selected Mechanic illustration emphasizes human service context and repaired hardware. This is a visible era-cue gap only, not an engineering or historical claim.
